original_value: Agriculture provides for the most basic needs of humankind: food and fiber. The introduction of new farming techniques in the past century (e.g., during the Green Revolution) has helped agriculture keep pace with growing demands for food and other agricultural products. However, further increases in food demand, a growing population, and rising income levels are likely to put additional strain on natural resources. With growing recognition of the negative impacts of agriculture on the environment, new techniques and approaches should be able to meet future food demands while maintaining or reducing the environmental footprint of agriculture. Emerging technologies, such as geospatial technologies, Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data analysis, and artificial intelligence (AI), could be utilized to make informed management decisions aimed to increase crop production. Precision agriculture (PA) entails the application of a suite of such technologies to optimize agricultural inputs to increase agricultural production and reduce input losses. Use of remote sensing technologies for PA has increased rapidly during the past few decades. The unprecedented availability of high resolution (spatial, spectral and temporal) satellite images has promoted the use of remote sensing in many PA applications, including crop monitoring, irrigation management, nutrient application, disease and pest management, and yield prediction. In this paper, we provide an overview of remote sensing systems, techniques, and vegetation indices along with their recent (2015–2020) applications in PA. Remote-sensing-based PA technologies such as variable fertilizer rate application technology in Green Seeker and Crop Circle have already been incorporated in commercial agriculture. Use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has increased tremendously during the last decade due to their cost-effectiveness and flexibility in obtaining the high-resolution (cm-scale) images needed for PA applications. At the same time, the availability of a large amount of satellite data has prompted researchers to explore advanced data storage and processing techniques such as cloud computing and machine learning. Given the complexity of image processing and the amount of technical knowledge and expertise needed, it is critical to explore and develop a simple yet reliable workflow for the real-time application of remote sensing in PA. Development of accurate yet easy to use, user-friendly systems is likely to result in broader adoption of remote sensing technologies in commercial and non-commercial PA applications.

result.paraphrase: Agriculture meets humankind’s most basic needs, namely food and fiber. Over the past century, the introduction of new farming methods, such as those used during the Green Revolution, has enabled agriculture to keep up with rising demand for food and other agricultural products. Even so, further growth in food demand, population, and income levels is likely to place additional pressure on natural resources. As awareness grows of agriculture’s negative environmental impacts, new techniques and approaches will need to satisfy future food demand while preserving or reducing agriculture’s environmental footprint. Emerging technologies including geospatial tools, the Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data analytics, and artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to support informed management decisions intended to raise crop production. Precision agriculture (PA) involves applying a range of such technologies to optimize agricultural inputs, increase production, and reduce input losses. Remote sensing has been adopted in PA at a rapidly increasing rate over the past few decades. The unprecedented availability of high-resolution satellite imagery, across spatial, spectral, and temporal dimensions, has encouraged the use of remote sensing in numerous PA applications, such as crop monitoring, irrigation management, nutrient application, disease and pest management, and yield prediction. This paper reviews remote sensing systems, techniques, and vegetation indices, together with their recent applications in PA from 2015 to 2020. Remote-sensing-based PA technologies, including variable fertilizer-rate application systems in Green Seeker and Crop Circle, are already in commercial agriculture. The use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has risen dramatically over the last decade because they are cost-effective and flexible for acquiring the high-resolution, centimeter-scale images required for PA applications. Meanwhile, the large volume of available satellite data has led researchers to investigate advanced data storage and processing methods such as cloud computing and machine learning. Because image processing is complex and requires substantial technical knowledge and expertise, it is essential to develop a simple yet dependable workflow for real-time remote sensing in PA. Creating accurate, easy-to-use, user-friendly systems is likely to encourage broader adoption of remote sensing technologies in both commercial and non-commercial PA applications.
